title: Greenhouse Gas Auditing
desc: Measure, report and reduce greenhouse gas emissions for an organisation using recognised accounting scopes and data checks.
outcomes: Explain scopes 1, 2 and 3 and emission factors.
Collect activity data and calculate emissions.
Produce an inventory report and reduction plan.
task: Build a greenhouse gas inventory for one small organisation (practice case), with boundary, data, factors, hotspot analysis and reduction plan.
condition: A computer, a spreadsheet, public emission factors, two peers and a mentor. A practice dataset may be used.
standard: Boundary is stated; each number has unit and source; calculations reproduce; data quality is rated; plan has measurable targets; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Sustainability officers, finance staff, engineers, consultants in training.
evidence: boundary note, data sheet, inventory, hotspot chart, plan
modules: You cannot cut what you do not count.
Greenhouse gases trap heat; CO2 is the main one.
CO2e converts other gases to CO2 equivalent.
Reporting supports cost savings and customers.
Methane has a larger warming effect than CO2 per tonne.
Scope 1 direct; scope 2 purchased energy; scope 3 other chain.
Company vehicles are scope 1; electricity is scope 2.
Bills, meters, fuel logs, travel records.
Units must match: litres, kWh, km.
1,200 L x 2.68 kg CO2 per litre = 3,216 kg.
Efficient lighting cuts 8% for a payback of 2 years.
quiz: What are scope 1, 2 and 3?
Direct, purchased energy, other chain emissions. (Covered in module 1: Why measure. To pass that module: Peer understands.)
What is CO2e?
CO2 equivalent of other gases. (Covered in module 2: Boundaries and scopes. To pass that module: Written.)
Emissions formula?
Activity data x emission factor. (Covered in module 3: Activity data. To pass that module: Sources noted.)
Why record sources?
To audit. (Covered in module 4: Emission factors. To pass that module: Maths correct.)
Name a scope 3 category.
Purchased goods, travel, commuting or waste. (Covered in module 5: Scope 3. To pass that module: Method stated.)
Double counting?
Counting the same emission twice. (Covered in module 6: Data quality and checks. To pass that module: Issues logged.)
Why local factors?
Grids and fuels differ. (Covered in module 7: Hotspots and targets. To pass that module: Ranked.)
Why state exclusions?
Honesty. (Covered in module 8: Report and verify. To pass that module: Reproducible.)
How rate data quality?
High, medium, low. (Covered in module 8: Report and verify. To pass that module: Reproducible.)
How often update?
Yearly. (Covered in module 8: Report and verify. To pass that module: Reproducible.)
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: wind and solar basics, water management, biofuels.
local: Reporting rules and emission factors differ by place and year.
ladder: Why measure

L1: learner can say what CO2e means. Focus module: Why measure (Understand, 3 h). You cannot cut what you do not count. Key points: Greenhouse gases trap heat; CO2 is the main one. CO2e converts other gases to CO2 equivalent. Reporting supports cost savings and customers.

Teach: open with the worked example. Methane has a larger warming effect than CO2 per tonne. Then set the activity: Explain CO2e. Mark against the standard: Peer understands. Check at this level: What are scope 1, 2 and 3? Model answer: Direct, purchased energy, other chain emissions. Concept.
Boundaries and scopes

L2: learner knows scopes. Focus module: Boundaries and scopes (Understand, 4 h). Decide what is in. Key points: Organisational boundary: control or ownership. Scope 1 direct; scope 2 purchased energy; scope 3 other chain. Write what is excluded.

Teach: open with the worked example. Company vehicles are scope 1; electricity is scope 2. Then set the activity: Set a boundary. Mark against the standard: Written. Check at this level: What is CO2e? Model answer: CO2 equivalent of other gases. Scopes.
Activity data

L3: learner can collect data. Focus module: Activity data (Apply, 5 h). Collect clean data. Key points: Bills, meters, fuel logs, travel records. Units must match: litres, kWh, km. Record source and date.

Teach: open with the worked example. Fuel invoices give 1,200 litres. Then set the activity: Collect data for a case. Mark against the standard: Sources noted. Check at this level: Emissions formula? Model answer: Activity data x emission factor. Data.
Emission factors
L4: learner can calculate. Focus module: Emission factors (Apply, 5 h). Convert data. Key points: Emissions = activity data x factor. Use recent, local factors. Record version.

Teach: open with the worked example. 1,200 L x 2.68 kg CO2 per litre = 3,216 kg. Then set the activity: Calculate five lines. Mark against the standard: Maths correct. Check at this level: Why record sources? Model answer: To audit. Maths.
Scope 3
L5: learner can find hotspots. Focus module: Scope 3 (Analyse, 5 h). The big chain. Key points: Purchased goods, travel, commuting, waste. Start with the largest categories. Use estimates and say so.

Teach: open with the worked example. Travel is 22% of the total. Then set the activity: Estimate two categories. Mark against the standard: Method stated. Check at this level: Name a scope 3 category. Model answer: Purchased goods, travel, commuting or waste. Hotspots.
Hotspots and targets
L6: learner can lead an inventory. Focus module: Hotspots and targets (Analyse, 4 h). Where to act. Key points: Rank sources. Set reduction targets and dates. Cost the actions.

Teach: open with the worked example. Efficient lighting cuts 8% for a payback of 2 years. Then set the activity: Draw a hotspot chart. Mark against the standard: Ranked. Check at this level: Double counting? Model answer: Counting the same emission twice. Lead.
Report and verify
L7: learner can audit. Focus module: Report and verify (Create, 4 h). Share honestly. Key points: Summary, method, limits. Independent review. Update yearly.

Teach: open with the worked example. The report states excluded sources. Then set the activity: Write the report. Mark against the standard: Reproducible. Check at this level: Why local factors? Model answer: Grids and fuels differ. Peer audit.
